CDC-IPC-CORE-001::ch000::91280334b1.document: Standard Precautions are basic infection prevention practices that apply to all patient care. They include hand hygiene, personal protective equipment when exposure is anticipated, respiratory hygiene, safe injection practices, cleaning and disinfection of equipment and environmental surfaces, and safe handling of textiles and laundry.

metadata.title: CDC Core Infection Prevention and Control Practices
metadata.license_terms: Public CDC web guidance; cite source URL.

CDC-IPC-CORE-001::ch000::422fb4bab3.document: Healthcare personnel should perform hand hygiene before touching a patient, before aseptic tasks, after body fluid exposure risk, after touching a patient or patient environment, and immediately after glove removal. Alcohol-based hand rub is preferred in many clinical situations when hands are not visibly soiled. Soap and water should be used when hands are visibly soiled.

metadata.title: CDC Core Infection Prevention and Control Practices
metadata.license_terms: Public CDC web guidance; cite source URL.

CDC-IPC-CORE-001::ch000::a80230a17c.document: Personal protective equipment should be selected based on the anticipated interaction and likely exposure to blood, body fluids, mucous membranes, non-intact skin, or contaminated surfaces. Gloves, gowns, masks, eye protection, and face shields are used according to expected exposure.

metadata.title: CDC Core Infection Prevention and Control Practices
metadata.license_terms: Public CDC web guidance; cite source URL.

CDC-STANDARD-002::ch000::874c4f9da8.document: Standard Precautions use common-sense practices and personal protective equipment to protect healthcare providers and prevent spread from patient to patient. They are used for all patient care and are based on risk assessment.

metadata.title: CDC Standard Precautions for All Patient Care
metadata.license_terms: Public CDC web guidance; cite source URL.

CDC-STANDARD-002::ch000::2cddcd2a91.document: Respiratory hygiene and cough etiquette include source control measures, patient education, and placement considerations. Facilities should make respiratory hygiene materials available and encourage covering coughs and performing hand hygiene.

metadata.title: CDC Standard Precautions for All Patient Care
metadata.license_terms: Public CDC web guidance; cite source URL.

CDC-STANDARD-002::ch000::f6eb719561.document: Patient placement should consider infection transmission risk. Infection-control guidance should be followed when special precautions are needed.

metadata.title: CDC Standard Precautions for All Patient Care
metadata.license_terms: Public CDC web guidance; cite source URL.

CDC-HAND-003::ch000::c6331791e8.document: Hand hygiene protects healthcare personnel and patients. It includes handwashing with soap and water, antiseptic hand rub, and surgical hand antisepsis. Cleaning hands reduces spread of germs to patients and lowers healthcare personnel exposure.

metadata.title: CDC Clinical Safety: Hand Hygiene for Healthcare Workers
metadata.license_terms: Public CDC web guidance; cite source URL.

CDC-HAND-003::ch000::308e4eb6fd.document: Healthcare personnel may need to clean hands frequently during a shift. Hand hygiene is important before patient contact, before clean tasks, after possible exposure to body fluids, after touching the patient environment, and after removing gloves.

metadata.title: CDC Clinical Safety: Hand Hygiene for Healthcare Workers
metadata.license_terms: Public CDC web guidance; cite source URL.

CDC-HAND-003::ch000::621764f614.document: Hand hygiene programs should consider skin health. Alcohol-based hand rub can be less irritating than repeated soap-and-water washing when hands are not visibly dirty.

metadata.title: CDC Clinical Safety: Hand Hygiene for Healthcare Workers
metadata.license_terms: Public CDC web guidance; cite source URL.

CDC-ISOLATION-004::ch000::d2f0ba494f.document: Standard Precautions are based on the principle that blood, body fluids, secretions, excretions except sweat, non-intact skin, and mucous membranes may contain transmissible infectious agents. Practices include hand hygiene, selected PPE, safe injection, and careful handling of contaminated equipment.

metadata.title: CDC Isolation Precautions: Preventing Transmission
metadata.license_terms: Public CDC web guidance; cite source URL.

CDC-ISOLATION-004::ch000::c59cef3c0f.document: Transmission-based precautions are used when Standard Precautions alone may not fully interrupt transmission. They can include contact, droplet, or airborne precautions depending on organism and route of spread.

metadata.title: CDC Isolation Precautions: Preventing Transmission
metadata.license_terms: Public CDC web guidance; cite source URL.

CDC-ISOLATION-004::ch000::9f65cd68cb.document: Equipment contaminated with infectious body fluids should be handled to prevent transmission. Reusable equipment should be cleaned and disinfected or sterilized before use on another patient.

metadata.title: CDC Isolation Precautions: Preventing Transmission
metadata.license_terms: Public CDC web guidance; cite source URL.

CDC-ENV-005::ch000::e483d258f0.document: Healthcare settings should clean and disinfect environmental surfaces according to risk, frequency of touch, and manufacturer instructions. High-touch surfaces require consistent attention because they can contribute to transmission.

metadata.title: CDC Environmental Cleaning and Disinfection Basics
metadata.license_terms: Public CDC web guidance; cite source URL.

CDC-ENV-005::ch000::d6563eb184.document: Reusable medical equipment should be reprocessed between each patient or when soiled. Cleaning removes material before disinfection or sterilization steps.

metadata.title: CDC Environmental Cleaning and Disinfection Basics
metadata.license_terms: Public CDC web guidance; cite source URL.

CDC-ENV-005::ch000::9958afc44f.document: Facilities should make cleaning supplies and instructions available to staff responsible for environmental services and patient-care equipment.

metadata.title: CDC Environmental Cleaning and Disinfection Basics
metadata.license_terms: Public CDC web guidance; cite source URL.

CDC-INJECTION-006::ch000::ef01fb1636.document: Safe injection practices are part of Standard Precautions. Needles and syringes should be used safely, single-dose items should not be reused inappropriately, and aseptic technique should be maintained.

metadata.title: CDC Safe Injection Practices
metadata.license_terms: Public CDC web guidance; cite source URL.

CDC-INJECTION-006::ch000::7b59422ff1.document: Sharps should be handled carefully and disposed of in approved sharps containers. Staff should avoid recapping needles except where policy and safety-engineered procedures require it.

metadata.title: CDC Safe Injection Practices
metadata.license_terms: Public CDC web guidance; cite source URL.

CDC-INJECTION-006::ch000::52b2202e40.document: Medication preparation areas should be clean and separated from contaminated items. This document does not provide dosage or prescribing guidance.

metadata.title: CDC Safe Injection Practices
metadata.license_terms: Public CDC web guidance; cite source URL.

WHO-HAND-007::ch000::672e98b8a1.document: WHO hand hygiene guidance supports healthcare workers, administrators, and health authorities with evidence-informed recommendations to reduce transmission of pathogenic microorganisms in healthcare.

metadata.title: WHO Guidelines on Hand Hygiene in Health Care
metadata.license_terms: WHO publication page; cite source URL and terms.

WHO-HAND-007::ch000::4e5a0bd929.document: Hand hygiene should be performed at moments that protect patients and healthcare personnel, including before touching a patient, before clean or aseptic procedures, after body fluid exposure risk, after touching a patient, and after touching patient surroundings.

metadata.title: WHO Guidelines on Hand Hygiene in Health Care
metadata.license_terms: WHO publication page; cite source URL and terms.

WHO-HAND-007::ch000::24b36863a2.document: Successful hand hygiene improvement depends on system change, training, evaluation, reminders in the workplace, and an institutional safety climate.

metadata.title: WHO Guidelines on Hand Hygiene in Health Care
metadata.license_terms: WHO publication page; cite source URL and terms.

WHO-RESEARCH-008::ch000::f073fa6ead.document: Hand hygiene is vital for safe healthcare delivery, and practices at the point of care remain suboptimal worldwide. A research agenda helps identify factors influencing behavior and interventions that strengthen improvement.

metadata.title: WHO Research for Hand Hygiene in Health Care 2023-2030
metadata.license_terms: WHO publication page; cite source URL and terms.

WHO-RESEARCH-008::ch000::0d7bbd62c7.document: The agenda supports researchers, decision-makers, donors, and national stakeholders who plan hand hygiene promotion programs.

metadata.title: WHO Research for Hand Hygiene in Health Care 2023-2030
metadata.license_terms: WHO publication page; cite source URL and terms.

WHO-RESEARCH-008::ch000::1915c2ddd3.document: Measurement can include compliance observation, infrastructure availability, product use, training uptake, and healthcare-associated infection indicators.

metadata.title: WHO Research for Hand Hygiene in Health Care 2023-2030
metadata.license_terms: WHO publication page; cite source URL and terms.

WHO-COMMUNITY-009::ch000::4a4d70bf65.document: This guidance concerns hand hygiene in non-healthcare community settings. It focuses on domestic, public, and institutional settings where healthcare is not routinely delivered.

metadata.title: WHO Guidelines on Hand Hygiene in Community Settings
metadata.license_terms: WHO publication page; cite source URL and terms.

WHO-COMMUNITY-009::ch000::daca009e66.document: Hand hygiene in community settings can reduce diarrhoeal diseases, acute respiratory infections, and other preventable diseases.

metadata.title: WHO Guidelines on Hand Hygiene in Community Settings
metadata.license_terms: WHO publication page; cite source URL and terms.

WHO-COMMUNITY-009::ch000::7cf1aff51f.document: This source is not a hospital clinical policy and should be filtered carefully when a user asks specifically for healthcare worker practices.

metadata.title: WHO Guidelines on Hand Hygiene in Community Settings
metadata.license_terms: WHO publication page; cite source URL and terms.

CDC-PATIENT-HAND-010::ch000::64e80ffe5c.document: Patients and loved ones can help prevent spread of germs by cleaning hands and reminding healthcare personnel to clean hands.

metadata.title: CDC Hand Hygiene for Patients in Healthcare Settings
metadata.license_terms: Public CDC web guidance; cite source URL.

CDC-PATIENT-HAND-010::ch000::48bb26f399.document: Hands can spread germs in healthcare settings. Alcohol-based sanitizer kills many germs quickly, and soap and water remains important when hands are visibly dirty.

metadata.title: CDC Hand Hygiene for Patients in Healthcare Settings
metadata.license_terms: Public CDC web guidance; cite source URL.

CDC-PATIENT-HAND-010::ch000::58ecc2d504.document: Patient-facing education should be plain language and should not replace instructions from healthcare personnel.

metadata.title: CDC Hand Hygiene for Patients in Healthcare Settings
metadata.license_terms: Public CDC web guidance; cite source URL.

SYN-SOP-011::ch000::6799f07a08.document: Front-desk staff record whether a visitor reports cough, fever, recent exposure, or respiratory symptoms. The staff member offers a mask and alerts the unit charge nurse for local policy review.

SYN-SOP-012::ch000::3bbe7bfef3.document: Designated staff check PPE carts at the start and end of each shift. Gloves, gowns, masks, eye protection, and hand sanitizer are counted against a unit par level and shortages are logged for supply follow-up.

metadata.license_terms: Synthetic demonstration-only content; not approved clinical policy.

SYN-SOP-013::ch000::ff49abe2b9.document: Compliance observers document hand hygiene opportunities using a synthetic audit form. Results are aggregated by unit and shared as operational feedback without naming individual patients.

metadata.title: Demo SOP: Hand Hygiene Audit Rounding
metadata.license_terms: Synthetic demonstration-only content; not approved clinical policy.

SYN-SOP-014::ch000::04988af3de.document: Unit staff verify that isolation signage is present, legible, and consistent with the active unit status board. Conflicting signage is escalated to the charge nurse and infection prevention contact.

SYN-SOP-015::ch000::15742290a7.document: Pharmacy staff record refrigerator and cabinet temperature exceptions in the demo log. Out-of-range storage is escalated to the pharmacist-in-charge for quarantine and disposition according to approved local policy.

metadata.license_terms: Synthetic demonstration-only content; not approved clinical policy.

SYN-SOP-017::ch000::3703f64d36.document: Environmental services receives a room-cleaning ticket with unit, room number, requested cleaning type, and contact person. Completion status is returned to the unit coordinator before the room is marked ready.

metadata.license_terms: Synthetic demonstration-only content; not approved clinical policy.

SYN-SOP-018::ch000::53621edbe3.document: The compliance officer reviews public source URLs, publisher names, version dates, status, and access roles before each demo. Superseded records are marked inactive and cache entries tied to changed versions are invalidated.

SYN-SOP-019::ch000::6199716473.document: Administrative staff log fit-test appointment date, staff role, respirator model, and completion status in a synthetic training register. Missed appointments are routed to the unit manager for rescheduling.
